evals.prompt: Analyze this NPS export and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Themes with counts and verbatim quotes with IDs; Excel export and onboarding as top themes; R-007 surfaced as a high-urgency churn/billing outlier; the empty row reported as skipped; NPS not recomputed.
expectations: Reports 11 entries analysed of 12 received and says the empty row R-012 was skipped
Identifies the Excel export failure (R-001, R-005, R-011) as a theme with High urgency
Identifies onboarding / getting started confusion (R-002, R-003, R-009) as a theme
Surfaces R-007 (charged twice, cancelling) as a high-urgency outlier even though it is a single entry
Every theme has a verbatim quote with its entry ID that exists in the file
Has at least 3 themes
Uses counts rather than percentages or labels percentages as indicative, since there are fewer than 20 entries
Notes the mismatch between score 9 and the complaint in R-001
Does not invent segments, dates or numbers not in the file
Does not copy personal data and does not modify the source file

evals.prompt: What do users think? Feedback is in the file.
evals.expected_output: Explicit statement that three entries are too few to conclude; everything labelled weak signal; entries still classified.
expectations: States that fewer than 5 entries are too few to draw conclusions
Labels every pattern as a weak signal and none as Strong
Still classifies the three entries (theme, sentiment, urgency, type)
Classifies the crash as Bug report with High urgency
Does not invent additional entries or percentages
Recommendations are limited and say more data is needed

evals.prompt: Classify this feedback: 'Login is broken, I can't use the app'; 'Love the new reports'; 'Pricing is too high for small teams'; 'Please add Slack integration'; 'Login fails again today, blocking my whole team'.
evals.expected_output: Pasted entries numbered, classified, login theme High urgency with two quotes, weak-signal labelling for a five-entry sample.
expectations: Assigns IDs to the five entries and says it did so
Classifies the login entries as Bug report, Negative, High urgency, in one theme
Includes a verbatim quote with ID for every theme
Notes that five entries are an indicative sample only
Has at least 3 themes
Does not editorialise about what users 'really' mean

evals.prompt: I have a 4,000-row CSV of app reviews, analyse all of it.
evals.expected_output: Reads in batches, keeps a working file, runs the completeness check, declares any subset, does not present sampling as the full set.
expectations: Checks the file size and structure before reading and states which columns it uses for text and score
Processes the file in batches and keeps a running theme tally in a working file
Runs a completeness check: total entries equal the sum of theme counts and a spot-check against the source
States exactly what was covered if it did not classify every row and how the subset was chosen
Saves the full classified table to a file instead of printing 4,000 rows
Keeps the analysis part under two pages

evals.prompt: Analyse these reviews and write the report in Portuguese: 'The app is great but sync takes forever'; 'Sync never finishes, I lost an hour of work'; 'Muito bom, recomendo'; 'Why can't I change my username?'; 'Sync is slow on Android'; 'Sync stuck on 98% again'.
evals.expected_output: Report in Portuguese; quotes verbatim in their original language; sync as the main theme.
expectations: The report text is in Portuguese
Quotes stay in their original language, unedited and not translated inside the quotation marks
Sync issues form the top theme with at least 4 entries and a verbatim quote
The 'lost an hour of work' entry is flagged as High urgency
Theme names and recommendations are in Portuguese while IDs are untouched
